S1.why: Short label under the bracket; 'libre' is the everyday Filipino word for free and reads as 'the free ones'.

S2.why: Imperative invitation to carry on; no limit or warning word, and fits 20 characters where 'Mag-save pa nang marami' would not.

S3.s: Nagamit mo na ang lahat ng %lld libreng cutling. Mananatiling libre at gumagana ang mga ito.
S3.back: Used you already the all of 5 free cutling. Will-remain free and working the [plural] these.
S3.why: 'Cutling' lowercase mid-sentence as the vocab's sync sentence writes it; 'ang mga ito' for things instead of the person-only 'sila'; 89 of 90.

S4.why: Says the first five cost nothing, which is also the promise they stay free; 'mo' keeps the vocab's informal-respectful address.

S5.s: Nagamit mo na ang %lld sa %lld libreng cutling.
S5.back: Used you already the 3 of 5 free cutling.
S5.why: '3 sa 5' is how Filipino says 3 of 5; the numbers come in the same order as the brief, so no positional forms are needed.

S6.why: 'Kasya' (fits) is the native way to say there is room for, and keeps the line at 23 characters with 5,000.

S7.s: Makakapag-save ka ng hanggang %@ text at %lld larawan.
S7.back: Can-save you of up-to 5,000 text and 500 image.
S7.why: 'text' and 'larawan' are the vocab's words for the two kinds; no plural marker after a number, as Filipino counts.

S8.why: Filipino lists three with a comma and 'at', no comma before 'at'.

S9.s: Sakop ng iisang pagbili ang bawat device sa iyong Apple Account.
S9.back: Covered by single purchase the every device on your Apple Account.
S9.why: 'device', 'bawat' and 'iyong Apple Account' come straight from the vocab's sync sentence; 'iisang' stresses one single purchase.

S10.why: What a Filipino says for a one-off price; 'lang' reassures, it does not push.

S11.s: Walang subscription, walang ads, walang sign-up.
S11.back: No subscription, no ads, no sign-up.
S11.why: The repeated 'walang' is the natural Filipino rhythm; the three loanwords are the words Filipino iPhone users actually use, matching the vocab's 'limit', 'device', 'naka-sign in'.

S12.why: The Taglish verb form used for this App Store action in Filipino apps; 'binili' (things bought) for purchases; 24 of 24.

S13.why: Progressive aspect by repeating the first syllable of the loan verb, the standard Filipino form; ends with the ellipsis character.

S14.why: Verb first, then the price as a single payment; 25 characters before the price, where 'I-unlock sa isang bayad na' would be 27.

S15.why: The same verb as S14 without the price.

S16.why: The everyday Filipino way to put something off without saying no.

S17.why: The plain imperative for closing a window or sheet.

S18.why: Warm and a little proud: everything, the room included, now belongs to the person.

S19.s: Salamat sa pagbili. Tulong ito sa Cutling at sa nag-iisang gumagawa nito.
S19.back: Thanks for the buying. Help this to Cutling and to the sole maker of-it.
S19.why: 'nag-iisang gumagawa' says plainly that one person makes the app; 'Cutling' capitalised here because it is the app.

S20.s: Maligayang pagbabalik. Nandito na ulit ang dati mong binili.
S20.back: Happy return. Here already again the earlier your bought.
S20.why: 'Maligayang pagbabalik' is the set Filipino welcome back; the second sentence avoids repeating the root 'balik'.

S21.s: Nagamit na ang %lld sa %lld libreng cutling
S21.back: Used already the 3 of 5 free cutling
S21.why: Spoken form of S5 without 'mo', since VoiceOver describes the row.

S22.s: May %lld cutling ka, at may puwang na para sa %@.
S22.back: Have 5 cutling you, and have space already for 5,000.
S22.why: Filipino nouns do not change for number, so '%lld cutling' reads right for 1, 2, 5 and 21.

S23.s: Naka-unlock na ang Cutling. May puwang na para sa %@ cutling.
S23.back: Unlocked already the Cutling. Have space already for 5,000 cutling.
S23.why: 'Naka-unlock' is the state form of the vocab-style loan verb; 'puwang' (space) as in S22.

S24.why: Says it did not go through without blaming anyone; 25 characters.

S25.s: Hindi maabot ang App Store ngayon. Subukan ulit maya-maya.
S25.back: Not reachable the App Store now. Try again in-a-little-while.

S26.s: Hindi kinumpirma ng App Store ang pagbiling ito.
S26.back: Not confirmed by App Store the purchase this.
S26.why: Puts the App Store as the actor, so the person is not blamed.

S27.s: Walang nabiling Cutling sa Apple Account na naka-sign in sa device na ito.
S27.back: No bought Cutling on Apple Account that signed-in on device this.
S27.why: 'naka-sign in' and 'device' from the vocab sentence; 'nabili' already means bought earlier, so no extra word for earlier; 74 of 80.

S28.s: Hanggang %lld cutling sa libreng bersyon. I-unlock ang Cutling nang isang beses at mag-save kahit ilan.
S28.back: Up-to 5 cutling in free version. Unlock the Cutling one time and save however-many.
S28.why: Two plain sentences Siri can say; 'kahit ilan' is the natural 'as many as you like'; exactly 100 with 5.

S29.why: Sits where the vocab's '%lld Cutling' count sits; '4 sa 5 libre' reads as four of the five free ones; 12 of 18, where any form with 'nagamit' runs over.

K1.s: Puno na ang %lld libre. I-unlock dito.
K1.back: Full already the 5 free. Unlock here.
K1.why: 'Puno na' (full) says the slots are filled without suggesting the items were used up; 'dito' (here) tells the person to tap; 35 of 38.

M1.why: Verb-led window title, as Filipino Mac menus name commands.

M2.why: Same command as M1 with the ellipsis character because it opens a window.

M3.why: Row label in sentence case like the vocab's 'Mga setting'; lowercase 'cutling' for the items.

M4.why: Compact pair in Filipino's own 'sa' form; 6 characters.

M5.why: State form, same word as S23 and M7.

M6.s: Isang pagbili lang para ma-unlock ang Cutling sa iPhone, iPad at Mac.
M6.back: One purchase only to unlock the Cutling on iPhone, iPad and Mac.
M6.why: Same list form as S8; 'ma-unlock' is the abilitative form after 'para'.

M7.s: Naka-unlock sa iPhone, iPad at Mac gamit ang Apple Account na ito.
M7.back: Unlocked on iPhone, iPad and Mac using the Apple Account this.
M7.why: 'gamit ang' (using) ties the unlock to this account as the vocab's sync sentence ties devices to it.

M8.s: Binili mo ang Cutling bago ito naging libre, kaya mananatili itong naka-unlock. Maraming salamat.
M8.back: Bought you the Cutling before it became free, so will-remain it unlocked. Many thanks.
M8.why: Plain cause and result with 'kaya', then a warm thank-you; 97 of 100.
